evidence.description: Option-based CEO measure requires two observations with options more than 100% in the money and becomes one from first qualifying year.

evidence.quote: we compute the realizable value per option as the total realizable value of the exercisable options divided by the total number of exercisable options.
evidence.description: Option moneyness uses realizable value per exercisable option and fiscal-year-end share price.

evidence.quote: the second overconfidence measure, OC_SZ, takes the value of one if the firm meets at least three of the following five criteria and zero otherwise
evidence.description: OC_SZ threshold and five-part decision rule.

evidence.quote: Excess investment is in the top quartile of firms within industry-years, where excess investment is the residual from a regression of total asset growth on sales growth
evidence.description: Excess investment requires growth regression residuals and industry-year quartile ranking.

evidence.quote: the industry is defined as a three-digit Standard Industrial Classification code.
evidence.description: Three-digit SIC industry definition used for OC_SZ criteria.

evidence.quote: firm has an OC_SZ score equal to one
evidence.description: OC_MSZ follows the first year the CEO’s firm has an OC_SZ score of one.

evidence.quote: we first estimate the firm-specific weekly returns for each firm and year because we are interested in firm-specific return crashes.
evidence.description: Firm-specific weekly returns are estimated separately for each firm and year.

evidence.quote: Specifically, the firm-specific weekly return, denoted W, is defined as the natural log of one plus the residual return from the expanded index model regression
evidence.description: Weekly firm-specific return is log one plus the residual from expanded market/industry index model.

evidence.quote: To estimate equation (1), we require that at least 26 weekly return observations be available for each firm and year.
evidence.description: Each firm-year index fit needs at least 26 weekly observations.

evidence.quote: fall more than 3.2 standard deviations below the mean firm-specific weekly returns over the entire fiscal year
evidence.description: Crash week threshold uses 3.2 within-year standard deviations below the firm-year mean.

evidence.quote: we calculate NCSKEW for a given firm in a fiscal year by taking the negative of the third moment of firm-specific weekly returns for each sample year and dividing it by the standard deviation of firm-specific weekly returns raised to the third power
evidence.description: NCSKEW is negative third moment divided by weekly-return standard deviation cubed.

evidence.quote: we separate all the weeks with firm-specific weekly returns below the annual mean
evidence.description: DUVOL splits firm-year weekly firm-specific returns into below-mean and above-mean weeks.

evidence.quote: we use logit regression when CRASH is the dependent variable and ordinary least squares (OLS) when either NCSKEW or DUVOL is the dependent variable
evidence.description: Baseline uses logit for CRASH and OLS for NCSKEW/DUVOL.

evidence.quote: All the independent variables are measured in year t - 1.
evidence.description: All main regression independent variables are lagged one year.

evidence.quote: we also include their financial reporting opacity measure (OPAQUE) and its squared term as additional control variables
evidence.description: Both OPAQUE and its square are baseline controls.

evidence.quote: In all regressions, we also include industry and fiscal year indicators to control for industry and time fixed effects.
evidence.description: Industry and fiscal-year indicators are included in all main regressions.

evidence.quote: standard errors corrected for firm and year double clustering
evidence.description: Reported Table 3 standard errors are double clustered by firm and year.

evidence.quote: The average monthly share turnover over the current fiscal year period minus the average monthly share turnover over the previous fiscal year period
evidence.description: DTURNOVER compares current-year and previous-year average monthly turnover.

evidence.quote: monthly share turnover is calculated as the monthly trading volume divided by the total number of shares outstanding during the month
evidence.description: Monthly turnover is volume divided by monthly shares outstanding.

evidence.quote: SIZE The log of the market value of equity MB The market value of equity divided by the book value of equity LEV The total long-term debt divided by total assets ROA The income before extraordinary items divided by lagged total assets
evidence.description: Appendix control definitions for SIZE, MB, LEV and ROA.

evidence.quote: ONEPCT_OPT/(ONEPCT_OPT + SALARY + BONUS)
evidence.description: Option incentive ratio numerator divided by numerator plus salary and bonus.

evidence.quote: INCENTIVE_STK The incentive ratio for executive stock holdings, defined similarly to INCENTIVE_OPT
evidence.description: Stock incentive ratio is said to be defined similarly to the option ratio; no formula is given.

evidence.quote: The prior three years’ moving sum of the absolute value of discretionary accruals
evidence.description: OPAQUE is a prior three-year moving sum of absolute discretionary accruals.

evidence.quote: Daily Returns: July 1, 1926- September 30, 2026
evidence.description: Official Fama/French detail page lists daily 48-industry portfolio returns covering July 1926 through September 2026 and links TXT/CSV files.

evidence.quote: We assign each NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ stock to an industry portfolio at the end of June of year t based on its four-digit SIC code
evidence.description: Official construction description for the 48-industry reference series; its SIC-to-industry grouping is an unresolved paper mapping.

evidence.quote: Beginning with the January 2025 data release, we use the new Stock and Indexes Flat File Format 2.0 (CIZ) files to generate US research returns.
evidence.description: Official data library documents a current CRSP-vintage change for U.S. research returns; historical FIZ archives remain a separate vintage.
